- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.30) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.40), model often underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing upside.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model may lag; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); reduce first 5 days by 2–5% to align with observed lag.
- If sentiment history shows volatility + mixed sentiment (±0.20–0.30), model tends to overfit short-term noise; apply smoothing filter: average last 3–5 forecast points before final output.
